overall: Violation found: the Board failed to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals for about four and a half years and failed to review and release requested minutes by its next meeting; complaint on closed-session complaint review rejected.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to decide whether they could remain withheld; no review from Nov 2019 to May 2024.
allegations.key_passage: For approximately four and a half years, the Board failed to review executive session minutes to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted.

allegations.summary: After an April 24 request for 2023-2024 executive session minutes, the Board allegedly failed to review and release them by its next meeting on May 1.
allegations.key_passage: Because it did not review the minutes until May 21, and did not vote to release them until May 22, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant questioned whether the Board could review her open meeting law complaint in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: A public body may review open meeting law complaints in executive  session under G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(1) (Purpose 1).

remedy: Review minutes of all executive sessions held from 2019 to present within 90 days of the letter to determine if continued non-disclosure is warranted, to the extent not reviewed within the last three months.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; the Board was cautioned that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We now order the Board to review minutes of all executive sessions held from 2019 to present within 90 days of issuance of this letter to determine if continued non-disclosure is warranted, to the extent that it has not done so within the last three months, consistent with the guidance provided above.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
